title: Who did what
sub: The last film of Locks before the data, the first series of Data protection and privacy: a record of who did what, kept before anything goes wrong and out of reach of everyone in it, as David Warren's flight recorder kept a cockpit's last hours from 1954; the few alarms someone always answers; a copied session ended first, then read in the record; two emergency accounts for the day every lock jams; and a copy of the data nobody can delete.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look, Night glass: a dark hall of frosted panes, frosted where what's behind may not be read and clear where it may, with cards of near-clear frost and bright rims. Cyan is an identity, green allowed, coral denied or closed, amber power switched on and every alarm; a session or a key is always a sealed card of violet frost with a lock, never written out. Australia in the 1950s is painted in the same night light, with its place and year on a tag.
